name: CA-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Laura Friedman running with large financial edge
Republican challenger minimally funded ($58K raised, $2.6K on hand)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Friedman holds a D+21 seat, a decisive fundraising advantage, and no outside spending against her, while Meyers has almost no cash to compete. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
model.watch: A surprise would require a major late shift in the national environment or unexpected outside spending, neither of which is currently visible.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Laura Friedman, a Democratic incumbent, seeks a full term in a Los Angeles-area district that leans Democratic by about 21 points. She advanced to the general election and has raised roughly $828,000 with $469,000 on hand, while Republican Scott Meyers has raised under $60,000 and reports only about $2,600 in cash. No outside groups are spending against Friedman, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Friedman roughly a 97% chance of winning, and the district's fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-20s. With no public polling and a heavily underfunded challenger, this race is rated Safe Democratic.
